name: Cinematic voice-leading rule for pad/string layers: each two-voice layer alternates compressed seconds and expanded thirds, keeps one common tone between moves, and each new layer starts a perfect fourth, fifth or octave from the layer above, all inside one mode
goal: Write lush, emotional cinematic chord textures without analyzing harmony: build two-voice layers (strata) that alternate between a second and a third, keep one note held into each new interval, and stack further layers starting a perfect consonance (4th, 5th or octave) away from the layer above, staying inside one mode. Works for synth strings, pad voices or choir layers.

source.title: The only trick you need for Epic Emotional Cinematic composing

prerequisites: Any DAW or notation with a piano roll
Basic interval names: second, third, fourth, fifth, octave
A chosen mode/scale (the example is a modal F)

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: One scale/mode to stay inside (white-key mode works)

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: Number of strata (2-4 typical: e.g. high strings, low strings, woodwind-like line)

outputs.name: voiced_texture
outputs.description: Layered two-voice strata with prepared dissonances and contour

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Stay inside a single mode; you do not need to know the chord names.
Seconds are the compressed/dissonant state, thirds the imperfect-consonant release; alternate them.
Synth voices playing this keep steady pitch: no random pitch wobble; vibrato, if any, slow and tiny.
Composition rule only; renders with any pad, string or choir patch.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only pad before that.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Pick a mode and write the top layer as two voices that alternate a second (compressed) and a third (expanded), e.g. a second that falls out to a third.
steps.expect: A two-voice line that breathes in and out

steps.action: On each move, keep one of the two notes from the previous interval (a held common tone or preparation) and move only the other.
steps.expect: Each new dissonance sounds prepared and smooth

steps.action: Start the second layer a perfect consonance (4th, 5th or octave) below the top layer's top note, and run it in the opposite phase: where the top layer is compressed, this one starts expanded, and vice versa. Being less strict about common tones is OK here.
steps.expect: Two strata that interact, giving thick, counterpoint-like chords

steps.action: Add further layers the same way (e.g. a scale-wise woodwind-like line), each starting a perfect consonance away from the layer above. Let some voices move in parallel and some in contrary motion.
steps.expect: Rich, modal texture with contrary motion

steps.action: For a growing, expansive feeling, let the layers move wider and wider apart over the phrase.
steps.expect: The texture opens up toward the climax

steps.action: Assign layers to separate pad/string voices and listen; adjust by ear rather than analysis.
steps.expect: An emotional cinematic texture with prepared dissonances

verification: Every two-voice layer alternates seconds and thirds.
Consecutive intervals in the top layer share one held note.
Each layer starts a 4th, 5th or octave from the layer above.
All notes belong to the chosen mode.
